title: Missing tests never fail check --ci
assertion: In a git repository where `swerepo init --only ci --yes` wrote `swerepo-ci.yml`, with no file named `test_*.py` or `*_test.py` outside the folders pytest skips by default (dot-folders such as `.seamspec/`, and `build`, `dist`, `venv`, `node_modules`, `*.egg`, `CVS`, `_darcs`, `{arch}`) and under the project's `testpaths` when it sets them: `swerepo check --only ci --json` reports `ci.tests` as missing with `blocking` false and nothing blocking; `swerepo check --only ci --ci` exits 0, printing no annotation outside GitHub Actions and, in GitHub Actions, one `::warning` per non-blocking gap and no `::error`. Once a test exists under `tests/`, `ci.tests` is no longer reported.

origin.text: ADR-20261125-5f22 (the owner's choice, 2026-11-25): a project without tests is warned, never failed, by SWERepo's own report; its CI's test job still fails until a real test exists, and agents are told to write one. Gemini's review added pytest's own discovery (P8-G01). Checked by breaking it: the warning made blocking, skipped folders counted, the plan note dropped, and a warning never cleared each fail the rule. Refreshed on the owner's watchouts: structure only (the finding's status and blocking flag, the exit code, warning rather than error annotations, `.seamspec/` not silencing it), never English sentences; `init`'s plan note is covered by ordinary tests instead. Refreshed after SeamSpec's reviewer: the rule says what the code checks (named files, pytest's default skips, `testpaths`; not `python_files` or `norecursedirs`, as the warning never blocks), and `check --ci` exits 0 outside GitHub Actions too.
